params.script_inline:
import sys, json
# The door of a colony. The HTTP ingress puts the request headers into
# `context`; `hop` is empty unless the poster seeded one (GH #175), and no
# edge exists above the first cell that could name a lane for it. So this cell
# does the one thing a colony needs before any topology can act: it puts the turn on a named lane and
# promotes the channel identity, so everything downstream can screen,
# rate-limit and mint sessions PER CHANNEL instead of flattening them.
doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
d = doc["body"]
envelope = doc["envelope"]
header = envelope.get("header") or {}
context = header.get("context") or {}
hop = header.get("hop") or {}
channel = str(context.get("channel") or hop.get("chat_id") or "default")
sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
    "header": {"route": "turn", "chat_id": channel},
    "messages": d.get("messages", [])}))

description.purpose: The inbound surface of a colony: it turns an HTTP request into a turn on the ingress lane and promotes the channel identity, so screening below it rate-limits per channel and an agent above it mints one session per channel.
description.use_when: One per colony, as the first cell every inbound message meets. Wire exactly one edge out of it, onto whatever screens or receives turns.
description.not_in_scope: No screening, no session, no memory, no answer: it speaks inbound only, and outbound lanes end in a terminal instead.
